figures.shows: A 2 by 2 table of hardness results for classically simulating IQP circuits. Rows: noise-free, noisy. Columns: multiplicative approximation, additive approximation. Noise-free multiplicative: Hard (if PH does not collapse), cited to the 2011 IQP paper; noise-free additive: Hard (with stronger complexity assumptions), cited to the 2016 average-case paper; noisy multiplicative: Hard (if PH does not collapse), cited to Fujii and Tamate; noisy additive: Hard (general circuits, similar assumptions) / polynomial-time (random circuits).

papers.what_it_is: A theory paper showing that sparse IQP circuits on a square lattice are likely hard to simulate classically, that constant output noise makes anticoncentrated IQP circuits classically simulable, and that classical error correction restores hardness for any noise rate below 1.

assertions.value: The authors define an IQP circuit (instantaneous quantum polynomial-time) as a quantum circuit of the form C = H^n D H^n, where H is the Hadamard gate and D is a diagonal matrix produced from polynomially many diagonal gates.
quotes: An IQP circuit (“Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial-time”) is a quantum circuit of the form C = H⊗nDH⊗n, where H is the Hadamard gate and D is a diagonal matrix produced from poly(n) diagonal gates.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the term in Section 1.1.

assertions.value: The authors define the IQP sampling problem as sampling from the distribution on n-bit strings produced by applying C to the initial state of all zeros and then measuring each qubit in the computational basis.
quotes: The IQP sampling problem is to sample from the distribution p on n-bit strings produced by applying C to the initial state |0 ⊗n, then measuring each qubit in the computational basis.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the problem in Section 1.1.

assertions.value: The paper states, as a conjecture made in earlier work, that for random integer edge and vertex weights from the set 0 to 7 it is #P-hard to approximate the squared magnitude of the Ising partition function at omega = e^(i pi/8) up to multiplicative error 1/4 + o(1) for a 1/24 fraction of instances.
quotes: Let the edge and vertex weights be picked uniformly at random from the set {0, . . . , 7}.
Then it is #P-hard to approximate |Z(eiπ/8)|2 up to multiplicative error 1/4 + o(1) for a 1/24 fraction of instances, over the random choice of weights.
assertions.certainty_reason: A conjecture the paper attributes to earlier work, not proved here.

assertions.value: The paper states, as a conjecture made in earlier work, that for a uniformly random degree-3 polynomial over F2 it is #P-hard to approximate the squared normalised gap of the polynomial up to multiplicative error 1/4 + o(1) for a 1/24 fraction of polynomials.
quotes: Let f : {0, 1}n → {0, 1} be a uniformly random degree-3 polynomial over F2
ngap(f )2 up to a multiplicative error of 1/4 + o(1) for a 1/24 fraction of polynomials f .
assertions.certainty_reason: A conjecture the paper attributes to earlier work, not proved here.

assertions.value: The paper states that earlier work showed, assuming either Conjecture 1 or Conjecture 2 and that the polynomial hierarchy does not collapse, that there is no polynomial-time classical algorithm for approximately sampling from the output distributions of IQP circuits.
quotes: if we assume either Conjecture 1 or Conjecture 2, and the widelybelieved complexity-theoretic assumption that the polynomial hierarchy does not collapse, then there is no polynomial-time classical algorithm for approximately sampling from the output distributions of IQP circuits.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result attributed to earlier work.

assertions.value: The authors state that the earlier results assume that all pairs of qubits are able to interact.
quotes: The results of [11] assume that all pairs of qubits are able to interact.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this limit of the earlier work in Section 1.

assertions.value: The authors state (Theorem 3, informal) that there is a family of commuting quantum circuits on n qubits, and that a constant fraction of circuits picked from the family cannot be simulated classically unless the polynomial hierarchy collapses to the third level, assuming a sparse version of Conjecture 1.
quotes: Theorem 3 (informal). There is a family of commuting quantum circuits on n qubits where: with high probability
cannot be simulated classically unless the polynomial hierarchy collapses to the third level, assuming a “sparse” version of Conjecture 1.
assertions.certainty_reason: This is the informal statement; the formal one is entered separately as Theorem 3 restated.

assertions.value: The paper proves (Theorem 3, restated), assuming Conjecture 8, that there is a distribution D on commuting quantum circuits on n qubits such that, with high probability, a circuit from D contains O(n log n) two-qubit commuting gates and can be implemented on a 2d square lattice in depth of order the square root of n times log n.
quotes: Theorem 3 (restated). Assume Conjecture 8. Then there is a distribution D on the set of commuting quantum circuits on n qubits
2-qubit commuting gates and can be implemented on a 2d square lattice in depth O( n log n)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper proves the statement, conditional on Conjecture 8, in Sections 2 to 2.2; the condition is quoted.
assertions.reader_inference: The square root in the depth is printed as a lost radical sign in the text layer: the quote reads O( n log n).

assertions.value: The paper states, as part of Theorem 3 restated and assuming Conjecture 8, that a q fraction of circuits picked from D cannot be simulated classically unless the polynomial hierarchy collapses to the third level, where simulate means approximately sampling from the output distribution up to l1 distance epsilon.
quotes: Theorem 3 (restated). Assume Conjecture 8.
a q fraction of circuits picked from D cannot be simulated classically unless the polynomial hierarchy collapses to the third level.

assertions.value: The authors define a sparse IQP circuit by including, for each pair of distinct qubits, a gate across them with probability p = gamma (ln n)/n for a fixed gamma.
quotes: include a gate across those qubits with probability p = γ(ln n)/n, for some
Call an IQP circuit picked from this distribution sparse.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the distribution in Section 2.

assertions.value: The authors define each 2-qubit gate of a sparse IQP circuit as drawn uniformly from the four diagonal gates diag(1, 1, 1, omega^k) with k from 0 to 3 and omega = i, and each qubit's 1-qubit gate as drawn uniformly from the eight diagonal gates diag(1, zeta^k) with k from 0 to 7 and zeta = e^(pi i/4).
quotes: Each 2-qubit gate is picked uniformly at random from the set {diag(1, 1, 1, ωk) : k ∈ {0, . . . , 3}}, where ω = i.
Each qubit has a 1-qubit gate acting on it, which is picked uniformly at random from the set {diag(1, ζk) : k ∈ {0, . . . , 7}}, where ζ = eπi/4.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the gate sets in Section 2.

assertions.value: The authors state that sparse IQP circuits contain O(n log n) gates with high probability.
quotes: Sparse IQP circuits contain O(n log n) gates with high probability
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated without a separate proof; follows from the edge probability in the definition.

assertions.value: The paper proves (Lemma 6, proof in Appendix A) that for a random sparse IQP circuit C the expected value of the squared magnitude of the amplitude of all zeros equals 2 to the power of minus n, and that for a large enough constant gamma the expected fourth power is at most 5 times 2 to the power of minus 2n.
assertions.anchor: Lemma 6, Section 2, p.9; Appendix A, p.18
quotes: Lemma 6. Let C be a random sparse IQP circuit. Then EC[| 0|C|0 |2] = 2−n and, for a large enough constant γ, EC[| 0|C|0 |4] ≤ 5 · 2−2n.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated with its condition (large enough constant gamma) and proved in Appendix A.

assertions.value: The authors conclude the proof in Appendix A by bounding the sum, and hence the expected fourth power of the amplitude, by 5 times 2 to the power of minus 2n.
quotes: the entire sum, and hence | 0|C|0 |4, is bounded by 5 · 2−2n. This completes the proof.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's proof concludes the bound in Appendix A.

assertions.value: The authors state that, by the Paley-Zygmund inequality, for a large enough constant gamma the probability that the squared amplitude of all zeros is at least alpha times 2 to the power of minus n is at least (1 - alpha)^2/5.
quotes: for a large enough constant γ, Pr[| 0|C|0 |2 ≥ α · 2−n] ≥ (1 − α)2/5.
assertions.certainty_reason: Derived from Lemma 6 and the Paley-Zygmund inequality, with the condition quoted.

up to additive error = αβ/8 in 1 norm.
